extracted.intended_audience: academic economists and empirical researchers studying informality, taxation, and firm behavior (graduate students, policy analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating an applied empirical research project on firm informality using household/firm survey data and input-output matrices, including model testing, variable construction, identification, and robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey sampling description and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the sampling frame and design: ECINF survey focused on units with five or less employees; two-stage sampling stratified by state and geographic strata, then by income within strata; urban sectors randomly selected with probability proportional to households; 16 households interviewed per selected sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed description of screening (households screened for entrepreneur presence), clustering/stratification, and how multiple observations per household or entrepreneur are handled. Use this to justify external validity and to compute appropriate standard errors or weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample restrictions and cleaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude observations with entrepreneurs younger than 15 and observations lacking education or gender information; report resulting sample size (48,803 -> 48,701 -> ~48,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit exclusion criteria, give counts and reasons, and discuss potential selection bias introduced by these restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of key outcome: formalization (taxreg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalization is measured by a dummy equal to one if the firm is registered with the Brazilian tax authorities (Cadastro Nacional de Pessoas Jurídicas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alternative proxies (e.g., 'legally constituted firms') and correlation between measures (noted correlation = 0.98). Discuss why chosen measure is most representative for study purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and definition of explanatory variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and document all covariates: taxsub (forward tax substitution), largecl/smallcl/govcl (client type dummies), outsidehouse, n_worker (includes owner), revenue, otherjob, bankloan, education (categorical), age, gender, ho_num (number of rooms for homeowners), loginv/loginst, profit, logwage, clform and supform (client/supplier formalization measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide units, timing (e.g., October 2003), and any transformations (logs). Explain special cases (e.g., a few firms >5 employees due to lag or partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching survey activities to national accounts (classification matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Match ECINF activity codes (CNAE) to National Accounts System (NAS) sectors; when multiple NAS sectors map to a CNAE, assign weighted averages using NAS sector production value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mapping tables used, report any exceptions, and explain weighting choices. This is necessary to attach input-output technical coefficients to survey firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of input-output technical coefficients and output allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IBGE input-output 'use' and 'make' tables to compute inter-sectoral technical input coefficients and sectoral output destination measures (at 2003 current prices) and assign to each survey activity a vector of these coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State ESA/NA conventions used, reference data sources and year, and explain how these coefficients are used as controls or weights in constructing supplier/client indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of supplier formalization index
rubrics_metrics.description: supplierformali = (sum_j tcij × formality_j) / (sum_j tcij), where tcij are technical input coefficients and formality_j is the percentage of firms in sector j with tax registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that this index weights sectoral formality by the share of inputs a firm sources from each sector; note that it ignores large suppliers not present in survey and discuss implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of client formalization index
rubrics_metrics.description: clientformali = (sum_j oaij × formality_j) / (sum_j oaij), where oaij are output allocation coefficients from the NAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe interpretation (weighted formality of a firm's sales destinations) and limitations given survey coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and normalization of enforcement intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement information is the number of labor-regulation visits in a given sector and state (2002) normalized by number of persons employed in that state-sector (or number of firms in robustness checks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ministry-of-labor inspection counts normalized appropriately; construct supplier/client enforcement indices by weighting with technical coefficients or output allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Econometric specification for the probability of formalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate probit models for the formalization dummy 'taxreg' with two sets of controls: (1) state and sector dummies, and (2) state dummies plus derived output coefficients from National Accounts as controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare results across control sets, report signs and statistical significance, and interpret marginal effects. Explain clustering/standard error strategy (note: standard errors not clustered by urban sector because definition varied between 1997 and 2003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of economic significance
rubrics_metrics.description: For dummy variables, economic significance is defined as the regression coefficient divided by the standard deviation of the dependent variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both statistical significance and this standardized economic magnitude to convey substantive impact (example: formalization associated with 0.31 sd increase in investments per worker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression choices for other outcomes (investments, employees, profits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use OLS for investments and installations per worker and profits (with controls for manager and firm characteristics). Use ordered probit and Poisson regressions for integer outcomes like number of employees; report that results are similar across methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify estimator choice based on outcome distribution; check robustness with alternative nonlinear models and report consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction terms and sorting variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use education as observable entrepreneur quality and include interaction of education and formality to test model predictions (e.g., positive interaction coefficient consistent with theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret interaction coefficients carefully (e.g., how education modifies the effect of formalization on employment); perform alternative specifications and subsample analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing endogeneity of supplier/client formality (instrumental variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: To address simultaneity and measurement error concerns, instrument client formalization with average education level in the entrepreneurs' urban sector; consolidate client dummies into an aggregate lsgecl variable when using a single instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain instrument choice and exclusion restriction, report first-stage strength and IV vs OLS comparisons; note that single instrument handles one endogenous variable, so consolidation may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and testing of tax-substitution sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sectors subject to forward tax substitution (list of CNAE codes) and test interaction of tax-substitution with client-formality measures; hypothesis: tax substitution weakens or removes chain effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run interacted regressions and test joint hypotheses (e.g., sum of coefficients equals zero), report p-values (example: p = .0636 failing to reject at 5% for no chain effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness via policy variation (SIMPLES) and pre/post comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Use policy change (SIMPLES introduction in São Paulo 1998) and compare with a control state (Rio Grande do Sul) using ECINF 1997 and 2003 to assess impacts on formalization; include controls used in prior regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement pre/post (difference-in-differences-like) comparisons, report marginal effects (example: 5.48 percentage point increase) and discuss alternative explanations and parallel trends assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling measurement error in revenue and capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Model revenue and installations as imperfect measures: revenue = y + e_y, installations = k + e_k with measurement errors mean-zero and uncorrelated; use cross-section averages and asymptotic arguments (CLT, Delta Method) to estimate ratios of mean revenue to mean installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and justify measurement error assumptions, derive asymptotic variances for ratio estimators, and use subsamples (e.g., informal employers with ≤2 workers) to approximate unconstrained informal group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation of relative cost of capital between informal and formal firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate ratio ˜ri/˜rf using ratio of average revenue per installation for unconstrained informal vs formal firms; provide asymptotic variance V and use sample analogs and Ni/Nf->c to compute standard errors (example estimate: informal firms face interest rate at least 1.3 times formal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain selection of unconstrained informal subsample, compute standard errors from formula, and discuss assumptions (measurement error, comparability of samples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and handling of data limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize limited ECINF information on production chains and missing large suppliers; complement survey with input-output matrices and be explicit about which suppliers/customers are captured or omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how omissions may bias indices (supplierformali/clientformali) and report sensitivity analyses or caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of comparative statics and model implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use theoretical model simulations and lemmas to derive comparative statics (e.g., increases in tolerance µ decrease aggregate supply, pi(µ) increases with µ; comparative statics illustrated by Figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly link empirical tests to theoretical predictions, display illustrative figures, and explain monotonicity and uniqueness results motivating empirical hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear documentation of tables and matching supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and explain tables (Tables 1–13), report variable definitions, correlation matrices, and where to find NAS and IBGE tables used (e.g., 'Tabelas de Recursos e Usos' on IBGE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reproducibility by specifying data sources, variable construction details, and making matching tables or code available where possible.
